<h2>Description</h2>

<p><code>goAquaFlux</code> computes gas fluxes from chamber-based aquatic
incubations. The function partitions total flux into diffusive and
ebullitive components when bubbling events are detected. Bubbling
events are identified using high-frequency concentration variability
(typically CH4), after which the time series is separated into
diffusive and ebullitive segments.
</p>


<h2>Usage</h2>

<pre><code class='language-R'>goAquaFlux(
  dataframe,
  gastype,
  H2O_col = "H2O_ppm",
  prec = NULL,
  criteria = c("MAE", "RMSE", "AICc", "SE", "g.factor", "kappa", "MDF", "nb.obs",
    "intercept", "p-value"),
  Area = NULL,
  offset = NULL,
  Vtot = NULL,
  Vcham = NULL,
  Pcham = NULL,
  Tcham = NULL,
  use_bubble_detection = TRUE,
  bubble.window.size = 30,
  bubble_gas = "CH4dry_ppb",
  bubble.method = "mad",
  bubble.args = list(),
  ebullition.final_window_min = 30,
  ebullition.window_C0Cf = 10,
  diffusion.minimum_window = 30,
  return_df = TRUE
)
</code></pre>


<h2>Arguments</h2>

<table role = "presentation">
<tr><td><code id="dataframe">dataframe</code></td>
<td>
<p>A <code>data.frame</code> containing time series observations
for one or more chamber incubations.</p>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="gastype">gastype</code></td>
<td>
<p>Character string indicating the gas concentration column
to use for flux calculation. Allowed values include:
<code>"CO2dry_ppm"</code>, <code>"CH4dry_ppb"</code>, <code>"COdry_ppb"</code>,
<code>"N2Odry_ppb"</code>, <code>"NH3dry_ppb"</code>, <code>"NO2dry_ppb"</code>,
<code>"NOdry_ppb"</code>, and <code>"H2O_ppm"</code>.</p>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="H2O_col">H2O_col</code></td>
<td>
<p>Character string specifying the column containing water
vapor concentration used for dilution correction. Default is
<code>"H2O_ppm"</code>. If <code>NULL</code>, water vapor correction is disabled.</p>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="prec">prec</code></td>
<td>
<p>Numeric scalar specifying instrument precision for the gas
analyzer. If <code>NULL</code>, precision is retrieved from the corresponding
precision column in <code>dataframe</code> (e.g. <code>CH4_prec</code>).</p>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="criteria">criteria</code></td>
<td>
<p>Character vector specifying model selection criteria used
by <code>goFlux</code>. Default criteria include <code>"MAE"</code>, <code>"RMSE"</code>,
<code>"AICc"</code>, <code>"SE"</code>, <code>"g.factor"</code>, <code>"kappa"</code>,
<code>"MDF"</code>, <code>"nb.obs"</code>, <code>"intercept"</code>, and <code>"p-value"</code>.</p>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="Area">Area</code></td>
<td>
<p>Numeric scalar; chamber base area in
cm<sup>2</sup> (as in
<code>goFlux</code>; note the internal factor of 10,000 to
m<sup>2</sup>). If <code>NULL</code>, the
value is retrieved from the <code>Area</code> column in <code>dataframe</code>.</p>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="offset">offset</code></td>
<td>
<p>Numeric scalar; height between the water surface and the
chamber top in cm, used to compute <code>Vtot</code> as
<code>Vcham + Area * offset / 1000</code> when <code>Vtot</code> is not provided.</p>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="Vtot">Vtot</code></td>
<td>
<p>Numeric scalar specifying total chamber volume (L). If
<code>NULL</code>, it is calculated as:
</p>
<p style="text-align: center;"><code class="reqn">Vtot = Vcham + (Area * offset) / 1000</code>
</p>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="Vcham">Vcham</code></td>
<td>
<p>Numeric scalar representing chamber headspace volume (L).
Used only when <code>Vtot</code> is not provided.</p>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="Pcham">Pcham</code></td>
<td>
<p>Numeric scalar representing chamber pressure (kPa). If
<code>NULL</code>, atmospheric pressure (101.325 kPa) is assumed.</p>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="Tcham">Tcham</code></td>
<td>
<p>Numeric scalar representing chamber temperature (°C).
If <code>NULL</code>, a default temperature of 15 °C is assumed.</p>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="use_bubble_detection">use_bubble_detection</code></td>
<td>
<p>Logical; if <code>TRUE</code> (default) bubbling events
are detected using <code>bubble_gas</code> and, when <code>gastype == bubble_gas</code>,
the flux is partitioned into diffusive and ebullitive components. If
<code>FALSE</code>, no bubble detection is performed and only a diffusive flux is
returned.</p>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="bubble.window.size">bubble.window.size</code></td>
<td>
<p>Integer specifying the rolling window size
(number of observations) used for bubble detection.</p>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="bubble_gas">bubble_gas</code></td>
<td>
<p>Character string specifying the gas used to detect
bubbling events. Default is <code>"CH4dry_ppb"</code>.</p>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="bubble.method">bubble.method</code></td>
<td>
<p>Character; dispersion metric passed to
<code>find.bubbles</code>: <code>"mad"</code> (default), <code>"variance"</code> or
<code>"diff"</code> (rolling MAD of increments, robust to a diffusive trend).</p>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="bubble.args">bubble.args</code></td>
<td>
<p>Named list of additional arguments forwarded to
<code>find.bubbles</code> (e.g. <code>list(k = 5, min_magnitude = 10)</code>).
Values here override the defaults for advanced tuning.</p>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="ebullition.final_window_min">ebullition.final_window_min</code></td>
<td>
<p>Minimum time window (minutes) required
after the last bubble event to define the incubation end for ebullition
flux calculation.</p>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="ebullition.window_C0Cf">ebullition.window_C0Cf</code></td>
<td>
<p>Time window (minutes) used to compute
initial and final concentrations for the endpoint flux estimate.</p>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="diffusion.minimum_window">diffusion.minimum_window</code></td>
<td>
<p>Minimum number of observations required
to compute diffusive flux before the first bubble event.</p>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="return_df">return_df</code></td>
<td>
<p>Logical. If <code>TRUE</code> (default) the function returns a
tidy list of three data frames (see <strong>Value</strong>). If <code>FALSE</code>, the
raw per-incubation results list is returned instead, which is convenient
for advanced users who want the untidied intermediate objects.</p>
</td></tr>
</table>


<h2>Details</h2>

<p>The workflow includes:
</p>

<ol>
<li><p> Data validation and cleaning
</p>
</li>
<li><p> Calculation of auxiliary variables (flux conversion term and MDF)
</p>
</li>
<li><p> Bubble detection (typically using CH4 concentration)
</p>
</li>
<li><p> Estimation of ebullition flux based on detected bubble magnitudes
</p>
</li>
<li><p> Estimation of diffusive flux using model selection
</p>
</li>
<li><p> Combination of diffusive and ebullitive components into total flux
</p>
</li></ol>

<p>The function operates on datasets containing multiple chamber
incubations, which are automatically split using the <code>UniqueID</code>
column.
</p>
<p>Bubble detection is performed using a rolling window approach applied
to concentration variability of the selected gas (typically CH4).
Detected bubbling events are used to estimate ebullition fluxes and
restrict the time window used for diffusive flux estimation.
</p>
<p>Diffusive fluxes are calculated using the <code>goFlux</code> framework,
which evaluates multiple regression models and selects the best model
according to user-defined criteria.
</p>


<h2>Value</h2>

<p>If <code>return_df = TRUE</code> (default), a named list of three data frames:
</p>

<dl>
<dt><code>flux_summary</code></dt><dd><p>One row per incubation, with <code>UniqueID</code>,
<code>gastype</code>, <code>flux_total</code>, <code>SE_total</code>, <code>flux_diffusive</code>,
<code>SE_diffusive</code>, <code>n_obs.diffusion</code>, <code>flux_ebullition</code>,
<code>SE_ebullition</code> and <code>first_bubble_time</code>.</p>
</dd>
<dt><code>bubbles</code></dt><dd><p>All detected bubbling events across incubations
(<code>NULL</code> if none), each tagged with its <code>UniqueID</code>.</p>
</dd>
<dt><code>diffusive</code></dt><dd><p>The selected diffusive-model row (from
<code>best.flux</code>) per incubation, tagged with
<code>UniqueID</code>.</p>
</dd>
</dl>

<p>If <code>return_df = FALSE</code>, the raw per-incubation results list is returned.
</p>
<p>Flux units follow <code>goFlux</code>:
µmol m<sup>-2</sup>s<sup>-1</sup>
for ppm gases and
nmol m<sup>-2</sup>s<sup>-1</sup>
for ppb gases.
</p>
